locator: Current Biology31,R233–R234; both PDF pages and Figure1
inspectedText: The original two-page research report documents two Elysia taxa shedding the main body, including the heart. Three relatively young E.cf.marginata heads fed within hours and regrew bodies in roughly20days; two older heads did not feed and died. In E.atroviridis, parasites were associated with shedding and removed in surviving regenerated animals; parasite-free animals did not shed during observation. Authors propose parasite removal as a function and kleptoplasty as support, but explicitly state the survival and regeneration mechanism remains unclear. Photosynthesis is not established here as the causal explanation of head survival. Other alternatives are acknowledged. The evidence supports an extraordinary observed capacity with bounded sample/age/species limits, not immortality or a human regenerative treatment.
inspectionExtent: Main report complete; supplementary experiments/video not inspected.
